shadow:
The wanting never closes. You get the thing, and for an afternoon it holds, and then the wanting reopens and looks for the next thing. This is the engine that built cities and lifted families out of mud. It is not a flaw in the wiring. It is the wiring doing exactly what it was made to do.

Greed is wanting without trust. The hand grabs because some old part of the body is sure that if it does not grab now, there will be nothing later. It runs on a fear of being last, of being low, of being the one left with empty hands while others climb. So it climbs harder.

Most people read this hunger as proof of a small or grasping heart and try to starve it out. That misses what it is. The hunger is fuel. It is crude, it burns dirty, but it is the only fuel that will ever get a person off the ground. The work is not to kill the hunger. It is to notice what it keeps reaching for, and to ask whether the outside thing was ever going to fill it.
repressive: Some people meet the hunger by deciding not to want anything at all. They begin things with fire, then quietly let the goal slip, telling themselves they were never that ambitious. The drive sinks instead of burning. It looks like peace.
reactive: Others let the hunger run loose. They chase the next acquisition, the bigger number, the higher seat, and stay angry the whole way up. More is never the amount. The grasping closes the heart while the pile keeps growing.
gift:
One day a person sees that no outside thing has ever filled the hole, and stops sending the hunger outward. The same fuel is still there. It just turns and starts pointing up instead of out.

That turning is aspiration. The word shares a root with breathing. You draw the crude fuel in, and something in you begins to refine it, so the wanting that used to chase a car now reaches for something it cannot name and senses anyway. It is wider than ambition.

The question that opens here is plain and it cuts clean. How does what I have move to where it is needed. A person living in this Gift starts noticing that hoarded energy goes stale, that money and attention and care all want to stay liquid, flowing between people rather than frozen in one account. They begin to climb in a way that pulls others up the slope behind them, because a climb that strands everyone else stops being worth the height. There is danger here. Reaching too hard, too fast, before the body is ready, can short the circuit. The ground keeps calling this energy back down, and it should.
siddhi:
Deep in the work, wanting is no longer something a person has. It has become the current itself, and the current only runs one direction now, which is up and home.

This is the path of the long climb, the one with no step you get to skip. Every hard thing has to pass through and be changed inside the body. The serpent at the base of the spine uncoils slow, and what looks like fire is closer to liquid fire, the body steamed clean of old memory until what is left is translucent.

The hunger is not killed. It is worn smooth, the way wind works a hard rock down into something soft and round over a very long time. The grasping that started the whole thing was never the enemy. It was the booster, the crude first stage, the only thing with enough thrust to break a life free of the ground it was stuck to. A person can look back from the height and see the greedy beginning for what it was. Not a low place to be ashamed of. The launch.
